covers: calls of tools defined with groundedTool or controlTool
does_not_cover: tools defined with plain defineTool; provider-executed tools; writes made by effects, hooks, handlers or endpoints
scope: one thread (threadId), executions ordered by the runtime
boundaries: a call outside an execution authorises nothing
concurrency_note: the runtime runs one execution of a thread at a time, and serially() orders the checks of one realm
host_gaps: A call that state.invokeTool() runs in another JavaScript realm is not serialised or attributed

A nested call is covered only when it consumes the composite's nesting token: a runtime that parses the arguments before the nested tool sees them, or runs it in a new execution, makes the call be checked on its own
Other code that calls a listed tool with exactly the arguments of a pending invocation, at the same moment, can take that invocation's one covered call
The thread's key-value store is writable by any code in the thread

The runtime parses a call's arguments with JSON.parse before the tool sees them: an integer literal beyond ±2^53 reaches the binding rounded, and it checks and digests the rounded value, which is also what the tool runs with
not_applied: §5.18.10 persist and audit rows (F504): the data a persist tool writes and the record an audit tool appends are not checked for a secret the layer recognises (§6.7); such a call is decided by the other checks alone
§5.18.10 send row (F504): no destination policy (§4.4.2) is applied, and a binding's destination member is loaded but not read; a send call is decided by the other checks alone

§5.18.10 transform row and the every-capability redaction row (§6.7): the trace entries the binding writes are not redacted (an output's evidence_anchors are copied into the trace as they are), nor is a transform output it records
